BLOCKER: Acceptance-required lifecycle conformance tests are missing: no S3 ApplyLifecycle/ObjectLifecycle test skipped-without-endpoint, and local ErrUnsupported capability is only exercised indirectly via Put, not via ApplyLifecycle/ObjectLifecycle.
MAJOR: Checksum mismatch is fail-open: comparison is skipped when either side's checksum is empty, so store-side checksum absence silently reports "clean" instead of flagging unknown/unverifiable objects.
LifecycleState omits versioning, which the AC explicitly lists as part of ObjectLifecycle(key); the capability contract is incomplete for long-term consumers.
Reconcile never calls ObjectStore.Head despite the AC specifying List/Head comparison; any field Head returns but List omits (e.g. checksum) can never be reconciled.
Security-boundary rejections (objpolicy ErrMethod/ErrTTL/ErrTenantKey/ErrUnsupported) and drift reports emit no structured logs/metrics, leaving the privilege boundary unobservable in production.
MINOR: Manifest keys outside the prefix are counted as "Missing" rather than rejected as an invalid manifest, corrupting Expected/Missing counts and weakening report semantics.
`AllowedMethods` is an exported, mutable map: any package can add DELETE/POST at runtime, undermining the fixed allowlist guarantee.
Tenant guard does no key normalization: `tenant-a/../tenant-b/x` passes the prefix test; use path-clean comparison before minting.
`LegalHold=false` is a silent no-op — there is no release path for legal hold, and the one-way nature is undocumented at the interface level.

LocalStore implements LifecycleCapable but `Lifecycle()` reports capability=true for it, forcing every caller to also handle ErrUnsupported; consider a positive `ObjectLock` capability flag (S3 already advertises one).
Two new single-purpose Go modules with local `replace` directives add build-graph/module sprawl; weigh folding into an existing module or a shared workspace manifest.
NIT: Duplicate manifest keys are appended twice to Missing and silently overwrite in `want`.
`ApplyLifecycle`/`ObjectLifecycle` on LocalStore ignore `ctx`/`key` parameters (minor lint/readability noise).
Error strings are duplicated verbatim across the two LocalStore lifecycle methods.
SUMMARY: Solid overall shape: optional capability interface, fail-closed mint policy with typed errors, and a read-only deterministic scanner are the right primitives. Top risks are a missing acceptance-required test, a checksum fail-open path that can certify unverified data as clean, and an incomplete/observable-less lifecycle contract — all of which undercut the integrity and compliance goals of BI-PF-1308.
